sections.label: Legal protection for casual workers
sections.summary: MP asks if MOM will study other jurisdictions' legal protection for casual workers, who were 3.4% of resident employees in 2018, down from 5.1% in 2009, and are covered by laws like the Employment Act and CPF Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry can conduct an in-depth study on legal protection for casual workers in other jurisdictions with the view of developing a new framework on the rights and benefits of casual workers, given the rise in number of such workers in recent years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: They constituted 3.4% of resident employees in 2018, down from 5.1% in 2009.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: All employees, including casual work employees, are covered by Singapore’s various employment-related legislation, such as the Employment Act and Central Provident Fund (CPF) Act.

sections.label: Contribute-As-You-Earn for SEPs
sections.summary: A "Contribute-As-You-Earn" model will be introduced to make it easier for SEPs to save for their healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Lastly, we will be introducing a "Contribute-As-You-Earn" model to make it easier for SEPs to save for their healthcare needs.

sections.label: Assessed risk of separate worker category
sections.summary: Some jurisdictions introduced a separate worker category with limited employment protection, but it was assessed this could lead employers to reclassify existing employees, reducing protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: We are aware of some jurisdictions that introduced a separate category of workers and some limited employment protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But we assessed that doing so could lead employers to reclassify existing employees under this separate category, resulting in reduced protection.

sections.label: Misclassification cases and repayments
sections.summary: In the last three years MOM and CPF Board received 308 suspected misclassification cases; 160 workers were assessed misclassified, about 100 a year, and in all but two cases employers made good their obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In the last three years, MOM and CPF Board received a total of 308 cases of suspected misclassification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In 160 cases, workers were assessed to be misclassified as SEPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: On average, about 100 workers a year were found to be misclassified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In all but two of these misclassification cases, employers made good their obligations when informed of the misclassification and paid back the affected employees what they were due, including overtime pay and CPF contribution.
